summary: Fifteen English sentences about family members and professions to translate into Finnish using genitive pronouns and nouns, with a vocabulary list.
transcript:
MINUN SISKONI ON HAMMASLÄÄKÄRI. HÄNELLÄ ON PALJON TÖITÄ.
MY SISTER IS A DENTIST. SHE HAS A LOT OF WORK.
THE GENITIVE: MINUN, SINUN, HÄNEN, MEIDÄN, TEIDÄN, HEIDÄN, OPETTAJAN, SUSANNAN..
TRANSLATE THE SENTENCES:
1. THIS IS MY BROTHER.
2. HE IS A POLICE OFFICER.
3. HIS WIFE IS A NURSERY TEACHER.
4. THEIR DAUGHTER IS 5 YEARS OLD.
5. HER NAME IS TUIJA.
6. HER TEACHER’S NAME IS SIRKKA.
7. HER TEACHER’S HUSBAND’S NAME IS JUKKA- PETTERI.
8. JUKKA-PETTERI’S FATHER IS FINNISH AND HIS STEPMOTHER IS SWEDISH.
9. HIS FATHER IS RETIRED.
10. HIS FATHER’S NEW WIFE IS NOT RETIRED. SHE IS A DENTIST.
11. IS YOUR FATHER RETIRED?
12. IS YOUR MOTHER A HOUSEWIFE?
13. IS YOUR FATHER BRITISH?
14. ARE YOUR SIBLINGS MARRIED?
15. IS OUR EXERCISE DIFFICULT OR IS IT EASY?
brother= veli police officer= poliisi nursery teacher= päiväkodin opettaja daughter= tytär teacher= opettaja husband= mies (WHEN ADDING ENDINGS, THIS WORD CHANGES INTO ”MIEHE-” AND YOU ADD THE ENDING AT THE END OF THIS SO-CALLED ”STEM”) Father= isä stepmother= äitipuoli new= uusi wife= vaimo dentist= hammaslääkäri housewife= kotirouva siblings= sisarukset exercise= harjoitus difficult= vaikea or= vai easy= helppo

lines.en: She has a lot of work.
